obligations.source_text: Create a single vertical social editorial photograph inside a heat-warped underground film-computation vault during an emergency archive salvage. Use the supplied portrait solely as a visible adult appearance reference: one visibly adult woman with long dark wavy hair, brown eyes, a neutral expression, a black blouse, and a small gold necklace. She salvages the final climate-model tape by bracing at a central recovery console while pulling a continuous translucent punched-film strip out of an oxidized brass logic wheel inches from the camera; the strip crosses her hands, threads through flooded calculation machinery, and reaches a blinking cold-storage tower deep in the vault. A very broad field of view spans the wheel, both side aisles, the centered console, and the remote tower in one rectilinear exposure. The near foreground appears relatively enlarged, with the brass wheel dominating the lower corner while the woman remains fully readable at mid-distance and the tower is tiny but distinct. Stretching increases toward the outer edges across the wheel rim, acetate strips, and side machinery, while her upright figure forms a stable central perspective anchor with straight central verticals. The phone-close camera position begins beside the wheel, and the unspooling tape creates a continuous foreground-to-distance action path. Green emergency strips cut through low sea mist, glinting on warped acetate, oxidized brass, and shallow water. Preserve realistic smartphone optics, tactile deterioration, documentary skin and fabric texture, and a coherent single-frame physical event.
